newsitem.title: FINLAND: Rallying metals, forestries lift buoyant Helsinki.
newsitem.headline: Rallying metals, forestries lift buoyant Helsinki.

text.p: A wave of demand for cyclical stocks, particularly metals and forestries, brought shares back onto an upward path on Tuesday in the wake of further gains in the U.S. overnight, leaving brokers carefully optimistic.
The HEX index put on 1.79 percent to 2,903.04 with volume at 605 million markka, heavier than on Monday but slightly quieter than typical levels so far this year.

"If nothing unusual happens in the U.S., this trend could continue," one broker said: but all noted that with U.S. Fed chairman Alan Greenspan due to speak this week, and New York last week showing mounting nerves, the market was hard to call.
Standouts included Outokumpu, which put on 4.60 markka to a six-month high of 90.00 as initial hesitation in response to its weak 1996 results on Monday gave ground to confidence.

"There's a lot of confidence in what Outokumpu said about recovering metals prices," one broker said, adding: "Hedge funds are buying metals." Other metals industry stocks Rautarruukki and Raute climbed in Outokumpu's wake and forestries, led in volume by UPM-Kymmene, put on just under two percent overall.
The FOX options index rose sharply to end just off a new life-high 1,024.86, at 1,024.24.

Among companies reporting for 1996, furniture and plastic pipes maker Asko was feted with a 24.00 markka or over six percent rise to 399.00 in lively trade after its earnings pleased and it set a five-for-one share split.

"They have made exemplary business sector arrangements and have a good outlook," one broker said, referring also to the arrival last year of Swedish furniture maker Ikea on the Finnish market: "Ikea won't ruin them," he added.
Nokia featured less heavily in overall volume but rose to overnight Wall Street levels, where it traded all day, and held gains after a higher U.S. open, ending up 6.00 markka at 307.50.
